items.title: Coprime torus knot

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Identify the standard oriented three-sphere with $S^3=\{(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2:|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2=1\}$ and choose $0<r<1$. The standard unknotted Heegaard torus is $T_r=\{|z_1|=r,\ |z_2|=\sqrt{1-r^2}\}$; its two sides are solid tori. In the angular coordinates $(u,v)\in(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^2$ given by $(u,v)\mapsto(r e^{2\pi i u},\sqrt{1-r^2}e^{2\pi i v})$, let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the first and second coordinate classes in $H_1(T_r;\mathbb Z)$. For coprime nonzero integers $p,q$, the **oriented torus knot** $T(p,q)$ is the image of $s\mapsto(r e^{2\pi i p s},\sqrt{1-r^2}e^{2\pi i q s})$, for $s\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, oriented by increasing $s$; it represents the primitive slope $p\alpha+q\beta$. The mirror convention is the reflection $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(z_1,\overline{z_2})$, which sends $T(p,q)$ to $T(p,-q)$ with image orientation, and reversing the knot orientation gives $T(-p,-q)$. For nonzero $p,q$ with $d=\gcd(|p|,|q|)>1$, the corresponding torus link is the union of $d$ disjoint parallel copies of the primitive slope $(p/d,q/d)$; it is not a single embedded curve of class $p\alpha+q\beta$. The exterior is $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ for a chosen closed tubular neighborhood. A positive meridian is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, and a preferred longitude is a degree-one class on $\partial E_K$ whose image in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is zero; this definition alone asserts neither existence nor uniqueness.

items.title: Unit-slope torus knots are unknots

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
references.locator: Remark 5.1.1 and Corollary 5.2.3, printed pp. 26 and 29

references.title: Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $p,q$ are coprime nonzero integers and $|p|=1$ or $|q|=1$, then the oriented torus knot $T(p,q)$ is ambient isotopic in $S^3$ to the standard unknot with its standard orientation.

items.title: Sign changes of torus-knot parameters give mirror and reversal

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For coprime nonzero integers $p,q$, the fixed orientation-reversing reflection used for the mirror convention sends the oriented curve $T(p,q)$ to the image-oriented curve $T(p,-q)$, and reversing the orientation of $T(p,q)$ gives $T(-p,-q)$.

items.title: A positive Hopf-plumbed surface for a torus knot

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory
Selman Akbulut and Burak Ozbagci, Lefschetz Fibrations on Compact Stein Surfaces
references.locator: §2, Theorem 1 and the gate-by-gate Hopf-plumbing construction, printed pp. 324–326

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $p,q\ge2$ be coprime integers. There is a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface $F_{p,q}\subset S^3$ whose oriented boundary is $T(p,q)$ and whose genus is $(p-1)(q-1)/2$. It can be constructed from a disk by plumbing $(p-1)(q-1)$ positive Hopf bands: a positive Hopf band is the oriented annulus spanning the positively linked Hopf link, and plumbing along a square glues square neighborhoods of properly embedded arcs in two surfaces on opposite sides of a 3-ball, with the four boundary edges alternating between the surfaces and with orientations agreeing on the square. For a connected compact oriented surface with one boundary component, genus is defined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$.

items.title: Torus-knot exterior group and peripheral system

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
Allen Hatcher, Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology
references.locator: §1.2, printed pp. 13–14, model Seifert fibers and multiplicities

references.title: Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory
references.locator: §4.2, printed pp. 34–37, knot-group presentations and abelianization

items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $p,q$ be coprime nonzero integers, let $K=T(p,q)$ be the oriented primitive slope curve in the standard Heegaard torus, and let $\rho_t(z_1,z_2)=(e^{2\pi i p t}z_1,e^{2\pi i q t}z_2)$ be the weighted circle action on the unit $S^3\subset\mathbb C^2$. Choose $N(K)$ to be a sufficiently small closed metric tube around the orbit $K$ for the round metric; this tube is invariant because $\rho_t$ is isometric and preserves $K$. Set $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$. Let $x$ and $y$ be based generators of the fundamental groups of the two solid-torus pieces obtained by cutting $E_K$ along the annulus left on the Heegaard torus, oriented so that the annulus core maps to $x^p$ and $y^q$. Then

$$\pi_1(E_K)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle.$$

The common element $h=x^p=y^q$ is central and represents a regular fiber of a Seifert fibration of $E_K$ over a disk. The fibration has two distinguished core fibers of multiplicities $|p|$ and $|q|$; a fiber of multiplicity one is regular, and a fiber of multiplicity greater than one is exceptional. Thus there are exactly two exceptional fibers when $|p|,|q|>1$, and one is regular when one absolute parameter is $1$.

For any integers $\alpha,\beta$ with $p\alpha+q\beta=1$, compatible based paths identify the positive normal-disk meridian and preferred longitude in the peripheral system as

$$\mu=y^\alpha x^\beta,\qquad \lambda=h\mu^{-pq}.$$

Here the positive meridian is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, and the preferred longitude has degree one around $K$ and maps to zero in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$. Their homology classes form a basis of $H_1(\partial E_K;\mathbb Z)$, so both classes are primitive.

items.title: Alexander polynomial from the torus-knot group presentation

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory

items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $p,q$ be coprime nonzero integers and let $K=T(p,q)$. Choose generators $x,y$ for the two-generator presentation $\pi_1(E_K)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$. Let $P_{p,q}$ be the two-dimensional presentation complex with one vertex, oriented edges $x,y$, and one two-cell attached along $r=x^py^{-q}$. The assignment $\phi(x)=q$, $\phi(y)=p$ defines an epimorphism $\phi:\pi_1(P_{p,q})\to\mathbb Z$; let $\widetilde P_\phi$ be its connected cyclic cover classified by $\ker\phi$. Let $A_K=H_1(\widetilde{S^3\setminus K};\mathbb Z)$ be the one-variable Alexander module for the infinite cyclic cover classified by total linking, with $t$ acting by the deck transformation of the positive meridian. Put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ and define
$$\delta_{p,q}(t)=\frac{(t^{pq}-1)(t-1)}{(t^p-1)(t^q-1)}.$$
Then $\delta_{p,q}(t)$ is a Laurent polynomial, $A_K\cong\Lambda/(\delta_{p,q})$, and the Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K$, defined as a generator of the zeroth elementary ideal $E_0(A_K)$, satisfies $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\delta_{p,q}(t)$, where $f\doteq g$ means $f=\pm t^k g$ for some integer $k$.

items.title: Torus-knot Alexander polynomial and genus formulas

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory
Selman Akbulut and Burak Ozbagci, Lefschetz Fibrations on Compact Stein Surfaces

items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $p,q$ be coprime nonzero integers, let $K=T(p,q)$, and put $a=|p|$, $b=|q|$. For $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, define
$$\delta_{a,b}(t)=\frac{(t^{ab}-1)(t-1)}{(t^a-1)(t^b-1)}.$$
Then $\delta_{a,b}(t)$ is a polynomial in $\mathbb Z[t]$, the Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K$ defined as a generator of the zeroth elementary ideal of the positive-meridian infinite-cyclic-cover module satisfies $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\delta_{a,b}(t)$, and the knot genus is $g(K)=(a-1)(b-1)/2$. Here $f\doteq g$ means $f=\pm t^k g$ for some integer $k$.

title: Torus knots and Seifert-fibered exteriors — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Worked cases of torus knots

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory

items.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. For $T(2,3)$, the exterior group is $\langle x,y\mid x^2=y^3\rangle$, a central fiber is $h=x^2=y^3$, a positive meridian is $\mu=y^2x^{-1}$, and a preferred longitude is $\lambda=h\mu^{-6}$. Its Alexander polynomial is $\Delta(t)\doteq t^2-t+1$ and its genus is $1$. For $T(1,5)$, the group presentation reduces to $\mathbb Z$, the knot is the unknot, the Alexander polynomial is $1$, and the genus is $0$.

items.title: Noncoprime torus slopes can be links

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes

items.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. The claim that every nonzero integer pair $(p,q)$ determines a single torus knot and satisfies the coprime torus-knot genus formula is false: $(p,q)=(2,2)$ determines a two-component link.
